mission: LÉLU 2.1 — geometry fidelity and mathematical validation
observed: Five samplers at n=800 on four surfaces: hair roots: A 0.3925 → E-hybrid 0.0968 (coverage 100.0%); surface detail placement: A 0.3943 → E-hybrid 0.0885 (coverage 100.0%); jewelry (diadem): A 0.4092 → C-vogel 0.0382 (coverage 100.0%); procedural surface sampling: A 0.0519 → B-fibonacci 0.0277 (coverage 100.0%). The one-arm logarithmic spiral was rejected on every surface for coverage (7–23%).
studied: Equal-area point distributions: ordered stride, Fibonacci sphere, Vogel disc, one-arm logarithmic spiral, and an area-even hybrid. The relevant principle is that equal spacing and equal area are different objectives (Vogel 1979; Bridson 2007).
question: Which sampling law produces the most uniform distribution for her actual surfaces?
hypothesis: One golden-ratio law is best everywhere.
method: Identical point cloud, n=800, same seed and same coverage radius per surface; measure spacing CV, min/max spacing and coverage; reject any method whose coverage falls below the surface it is supposed to cover.
results: hair roots: A 0.3925 → E-hybrid 0.0968 (coverage 100.0%); surface detail placement: A 0.3943 → E-hybrid 0.0885 (coverage 100.0%); jewelry (diadem): A 0.4092 → C-vogel 0.0382 (coverage 100.0%); procedural surface sampling: A 0.0519 → B-fibonacci 0.0277 (coverage 100.0%). Curls: the log law is the regular one (R² 1.000, growth 0.618/turn), while the hybrid has diameter CV 0.153 but R² 0.934.

evidence.note: per-surface methods with spacing, coverage and decisions
guards equal n, coverage and the rejected spiral

learned: There is no single winner. A surface thin enough to be one strip (the disc) favours Vogel; a closed sphere favours Fibonacci; an irregular anatomical cloud favours the area-even hybrid. The constant is not the answer — the surface is.
limitations: Four surfaces only; the accessory and jewellery surfaces were not sampled.
CV is a spacing statistic, not a perceptual one.
applications: Hair roots and surface detail keep the hybrid; the ornament disc keeps Vogel.
The matrix is the harness any new sampler must beat at equal n.
nextQuestions: Does the hybrid stay ahead on the accessory and jewellery surfaces?
Can the hybrid be made deterministic across resolutions without losing its coverage guarantee?
answers: Which sampling law produces the most uniform distribution for her actual surfaces?

assumptions.statement: a golden-ratio law is best on every surface
the one-arm spiral is usable if its CV is low
